subject: Cooking
title: Third Wave Coffee: The Craft Revolution
description: A short lesson to help you apply Third Wave Coffee: The Craft Revolution.

hook.text: Third-wave coffee treats beans like wine — origin, altitude, processing, and variety all matter intensely.

buildup.text: First wave: commodity coffee (Folgers). Second wave: quality chains (Starbucks). Third wave: artisan craft.

discovery.text: Third-wave roasters buy directly from farms, roast lighter to preserve origin flavors, and brew with precision.

twist.text: A single-origin Gesha coffee from Panama sold for $1,300 per pound at auction — the wine-ification of coffee.

climax.text: Cities like Melbourne, Oslo, and Portland became third-wave capitals — cafés outnumbering pubs in some neighborhoods.

punchline.text: Third-wave coffee isn't snobby. It's just paying attention to what others ignored.

quiz.question: What distinguishes third-wave coffee from earlier waves?
options: Focus on origin, artisan roasting, and direct farm relationships

details.summary: Third-wave coffee treats beans as artisanal products like wine — emphasizing single origin, transparent sourcing, light roasting to highlight terroir, and precise manual brewing methods. First wave was commodity coffee. Second wave was Starbucks-style espresso culture.
details.whyItMatters: Third-wave coffee recentered attention on quality, sourcing, and technique. It created a culture where coffee's origin and processing matter as much as the brewing method.
takeaways: Treats coffee as artisanal craft product with terroir like wine
Emphasizes single origin, light roasts, and transparent sourcing
Manual brewing methods like pour-over and Aeropress are preferred

faq.question: What are the three waves of coffee?
faq.answer: First wave: commodity coffee — Folgers, Maxwell House, coffee as caffeine delivery. Second wave: Starbucks-era espresso drinks — coffee as experience and customizable product. Third wave: coffee as craft — single-origin, traceable, light-roasted, manually brewed with attention to every variable.

faq.question: Why does third-wave coffee favor light roasts?
faq.answer: Light roasting preserves the unique flavor characteristics of the bean's origin — its terroir. Dark roasting overwhelms origin flavors with roast character. Third-wave roasters want you to taste the difference between an Ethiopian Yirgacheffe and a Colombian Huila, which requires lighter roasting.
